newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on export data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on export data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed sharply higher on Tuesday on surprisingly strong USDA weekly export inspections data and on speculation rains in Brazil would delay harvest, traders said.
USDA pegged export inspections for the week ending February 13 at roughly 35 million bushels, above trade expectations for 20 million to 24 million bushels.

Marketing year-to-date export figures for the period beginning September 1, 1996 were ahead of the previous year, USDA said. Soybean exports were at 574 million bushels, above the previous year's tally for the same period of 467 million.
Traders also cited talk that recent rains delayed harvest of early-maturing soybean varieties in Brazil and caused scattered damage in Parana.
Rains in Londrina in Parana state totalled 253.2 mm from February 1-17, already well above the monthly average of 180 mm, meteorologists Somar reported.
Soybeans closed 18 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher with March up 18 at $7.79 a bushel.
Funds bought at least 20 million bushels on the day. Refco Inc bought five million bushels May, three million March and one million July on the day, traders said.
Rosenthal Collins bought three million bushels May and Merrill Lynch bought three million March, floor sources said.
Volume was estimated by the CBOT at 76,000 contracts, against Friday's actual volume of 50,609 contracts.
